The warning about using the non-secret getter on a secret is commented out ("TODO[pulumi/pulumi#7127]: Re-enable the warning"), so reading a secret with `get` works and gives back an unmarked plaintext value.

verdicts.evidence: The tutorial passes `FileAsset("index.html")` as the BucketObject `source` (fn::fileAsset / fileasset in YAML/HCL). The linked target content/docs/iac/concepts/assets-archives.md has an `## Assets {#assets}` anchor that says: "An asset is a single file. Pass one to any resource input that expects a file, such as the body of an object in a storage bucket."
verdicts.framing_note: Link /docs/iac/concepts/assets-archives/#assets resolves to an existing page and anchor that describes FileAsset used for a bucket object body.

verdicts.text: You must use methods supplied in the Pulumi SDK to access an output's value once it is known.
verdicts.evidence: I checked this against a sibling page, content/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply.md, which says: "you cannot directly access or manipulate their values using standard language operations... The `apply` method solves this by waiting for the output value to become available." This fits how the SDK is built (outputs are async values read through apply/all). I couldn't confirm it in SDK source because the GitHub API hit a rate limit. One caveat: Pulumi YAML has no apply and resolves values through `${...}` interpolation instead.
verdicts.source: repo:content/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply.md (L15, L41); gh search code attempt hit a rate limit (HTTP 403)
verdicts.intuition_flag: The claim is broadly true for the SDK languages, but YAML programs read output values through interpolation, not SDK methods.

verdicts.text: Users can register their organization's templates in the Pulumi Cloud New Project Wizard for convenient access.
verdicts.evidence: (escalated from pass1) Pulumi docs say organization templates "power the New Project Wizard workflow." They are registered as template sources under Settings → Integrations → "Organization Template Sources." A Pulumi blog adds: "Pulumi Cloud Enterprise and Business Critical editions support registering your own custom templates for your organization which will be made available in the New Project Wizard."
verdicts.intuition_flag: The claim leaves out two things. Blog posts say registering templates is limited to Enterprise and Business Critical editions, and the docs say an org admin sets up the template sources. It isn't something any user can do.

verdicts.text: Once an ESC environment is set up and projecting pulumi configuration, that environment (or multiple environments) can be imported into a Pulumi stack.
verdicts.evidence: All three link targets exist and back the sentence: the linked ESC Pulumi IaC guide says "The `environment` block in your stack configuration file (`Pulumi.<stack>.yaml`) lists the environments the stack imports. Environments are merged in order", and outputs.md has a `## pulumiConfig` section, so the #pulumiconfig anchor resolves. The page now at L775 (the claim's L782-784 falls in the YAML block below it) rewords the claim without changing its meaning.
verdicts.framing_note: Linked guide: "lists the environments the stack imports" with a two-entry example; claim: "that environment (or multiple environments) can be imported into a Pulumi stack"

verdicts.text: The gke-secrets-encryption policy requires GKE clusters to have Application-layer Secrets Encryption enabled.
verdicts.evidence: The HITRUST Google Cloud policy data file defines gke-secrets-encryption with the description "Require GKE clusters to have Application-layer Secrets Encryption enabled". Its remediation sets databaseEncryption.state to "ENCRYPTED" with a KMS key. The claim transcribes this data accurately.
verdicts.framing_note: Generated-from-data page; the claim matches the data file's description word for word.

verdicts.text: The 'application-gateway-tls' policy requires Application Gateway to have secure TLS configuration.
verdicts.evidence: I checked the page's source data file. It lists policy "name": "application-gateway-tls" with "description": "Require Application Gateway to have secure TLS configuration", so the doc text matches the data it was generated from.
verdicts.framing_note: The claim restates the policy description from the data file word for word.

verdicts.text: Secrets have the same type, Output<T>, as unencrypted resource outputs, differing only in being marked internally as needing encryption before persisting in the state file.
verdicts.evidence: In the Node.js SDK, Output<T> (OutputImpl) has an `@internal` field `isSecret: Promise<boolean>`, documented as: "Whether or not this output wraps a secret value. Values which are marked as secret are stored in an encrypted format when they are persisted as part of a state file." So secrets use the same Output<T> type, and only an internal flag sets them apart.
verdicts.framing_note: Checked against the Node.js SDK only. Other language SDKs are assumed to work the same way.

verdicts.text: Go is one of the supported languages for this Pulumi AWS get-started tutorial.
verdicts.evidence: The official `aws-go` template exists in pulumi/templates (it contains Pulumi.yaml, go.mod and main.go), so Go is a real supported language for Pulumi on AWS. The tutorial's language chooser includes it (`{{< chooser language "typescript,python,go,csharp,java,yaml,hcl" / >}}`), and L46-51 list the Go prerequisites.

verdicts.text: This Pulumi program (as shown in the chosen language example) creates an NGINX deployment and exports the name of the deployment.
verdicts.evidence: (re-verified after own-file-only) This sentence only summarizes the page's own example programs. Every language tab in the file declares a Deployment with the nginx image and exports `name` from the deployment's metadata name (for example, TS `export const name = deployment.metadata.name;` and YAML `outputs: name: ${deployment.metadata.name}`). It says nothing about the product beyond what the example contains.
verdicts.framing_note: The claim describes the page's own example code, so the page matches itself. There is no external or product assertion to check.

verdicts.text: In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an `apply` callback is reported as a deployment failure, causing `pulumi up` to abort the update and print the error in its diagnostics.
verdicts.evidence: I couldn't check the Go SDK source because GitHub code search returned HTTP 403 (rate limit). The page also disagrees with itself: L631 says "In every Pulumi language, an unhandled error raised inside an `apply` callback is reported as a deployment failure", but the Go warning at L685 says an error returned from a discarded `ApplyT` output "is silently dropped and the update succeeds."
verdicts.source: repo:content/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply.md L631, L685; gh search code (HTTP 403 rate limit)
verdicts.intuition_flag: The page's own Go note contradicts "in every Pulumi language". The sentence should be reworded, for example to "in every language except the Go case below". Checking the Go SDK's rejected-output handling in sdk/go/pulumi would settle it.

verdicts.text: Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference, built from pulumi/pulumi source, confirms that the command publishes providers (executable plugins) to the Private Registry: "This command publishes a package to the Private Registry. The package can be a provider or a schema... When <provider> is specified as a local path, Pulumi executes the provider binary to extract its package schema."
verdicts.framing_note: The CLI page says a "provider or a schema" can be published to the Private Registry. An executable-based package is a provider binary, so the claim is a special case of what the page supports.
